## Core Overview
- Course Code: AIC372
- Course Title: Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR&R)
- Credit Hours: 3(3,0)
- Primary Purpose: Introduces the principles of logic-based knowledge representation, reasoning systems, and intelligent agent design.
- Fundamental Themes: Logic and semantics, uncertainty management, automated planning, and structured representation methods (frames, rules, ontologies).

## Key Concepts & Theorems/Formulas
- Knowledge-Based Systems: The role of logic in AI, declarative vs. procedural knowledge, and the relationship between knowledge and intelligent behavior.
- Structured Representations:
  - Object-Oriented/Frames: Generic frames, inheritance networks (strict and defeasible), shortest path heuristics, and inferential distance.
  - Rules and Production Systems: Working memory, conflict resolution, forward and backward chaining, and Horn clause resolution.
- Logic Foundations:
  - First-Order Logic (FOL): Syntax, semantics, interpretations, denotation, satisfaction, and logical consequence.
  - Resolution and Proofs: Skolemization, first-order resolution, Herbrand Theorem, and SLD derivations.
- Non-Monotonic Reasoning & Uncertainty:
  - Default Logic: Closed-world assumption, circumscription, minimal entailment, and autoepistemic logic.
  - Probabilistic Reasoning: Objective and subjective probability, Bayesian approaches, belief networks, and Dempster-Shafer theory.
- Advanced Topics:
  - Answer Set Programming (ASP): Positive programs, general programs, and calculating Hamiltonian paths.
  - Automated Planning: Situation calculus, STRIPS representation, progressive/regressive planning, and hierarchical planning.

## Exam Takeaways
- High-Yield Topics: First-order resolution and unification, SLD derivation mechanics, Bayesian network calculations, and default reasoning extensions.
- Critical Definitions: Know the differences between monotonic and non-monotonic reasoning, strict versus defeasible inheritance, and explicit versus implicit belief.
- Evaluation Structure: Midterm exam (25%), Quizzes (15%), Assignments (10%), and Terminal exam (50%). A passing grade requires a minimum of 50% overall.
